b:
The world
in the cruel grip
of corona

And there,
a crowd that mocks:
where is your God now?

The one whose mind
did not change
at the blood spilled
by the Syrian war,

the one whose heart
did not soften
at the screams
in the baby voice
of an innocent child
named Asifa,

the one who pushed aside
people wailing
every day
with no food to eat,

is he going to listen
only to your cries?

The one who planted the tree
may pour it water,
but he will not
hide the sun
with clouds;
it is the neighbouring tree
that gives it shade

In the same way,
for us too,
it is humanity
that will lend a hand

Keep humanity
in your hearts

After that there is no need
for temples of stone

There
we ourselves
will be God
note: Asifa Bano was an eight-year-old girl raped and murdered in Kathua, India, in 2018.
